body:
**Hands-on GUI check passed** (contributor, macOS, `test-429.camproj`, build of this head):
- Setup2's Setup page, **"Its own stock"**: the viewport shows only the setup's own stock box, with no teal.
- **"What Setup1 leaves behind"**: the page shows "Incoming from Setup1: X -15.000 .. 15.000, Y -15.000 .. 15.000, Z 0.000 .. 2.540 mm" and "Incoming volume: 2213.5 mm³". The viewport shows the **translucent teal incoming body**, faced and with the 6 mm hole, over the setup's own stock.
- Switching back to "Its own stock" removes the teal.

**Non-blocking cosmetic note:** the teal top face is speckled with the stock box's colour. That is z-fighting: the incoming body's faced top and Setup2's own Stock box top are coplanar, so the two surfaces flicker through each other. Possible later fixes are a small polygon/depth offset on the overlay, or drawing it after the stock with depth-test bias. It does not affect the stock math or any posted output.

Ready for review.

**Hand check finding** (contributor, M5 local build, 2026-11-09). This is a UX gap, not a crash.

**What happened:** with Setup2 set to **What Setup1 leaves behind** but holding **no operations yet**, the page says *"Incoming stock not known yet: the program never enters setup 'Setup2'"*, and the viewport shows no teal body.

**Why it matters:** `incoming_body` simulates the program up to the setup's first move. The moment a user most wants to see the incoming stock is right after choosing the carried source, **before** adding Setup2's operations, and that's exactly when the preview has nothing to show.

**Suggestion:** when the setup has no operations, compute the incoming stock from every earlier setup's operations, so the program state at the hand-over doesn't depend on the setup having moves. The verdict path can keep its current rule.

**Next:** the teal render itself is being re-checked with a project where Setup2 has an operation.

**Hand check FAILED: the teal overlay never renders.** Back to draft.

Contributor, M5 local build of #520 + #519 + #573 + #657 on main, real GPU (Apple Metal), 2026-11-09. The project: Setup1 faces a 60×60 stock (Z −2..18) down to Z 12, and Setup2 takes **What Setup1 leaves behind** and has its own Face2.

**What passes:**
- **Measurement:** Setup2's page shows *"Incoming from Setup1: X −30.000 .. 30.000, Y −30.000 .. 30.000, Z −2.000 .. 12.000 mm"* and *"Incoming volume: 50400.0 mm³"*. That's exactly right, so `incoming_shape` and the measurement path work.

**What fails:**
- **Render:** with Setup2's page open, no teal body appears, whether the view is Shaded or Wireframe, in the dark or light theme, and **with Setup2's own Stock node hidden** (eye off), so it isn't occluded by the setup's stock. Screenshots were reviewed in session.
- **Rendering was never exercised:** this PR's body already said "No real-GPU render of the teal", and the UI test checks only that a class-4 part is collected, not that it's drawn.

**Suspects to check:**
1. **The part is dropped by the traced or whole-program stock view.** The body's own "known limit" says that view replaces all stock-type parts, and it may be active by default when operations exist.
2. **`fs_stock`'s class-4 branch is unreachable** on the Metal path (the vertex class isn't carried, or is clamped).
3. **The part is collected but culled,** by visibility or because the incoming sheet's triangle winding or normals face away.

**Fix pin:** a GPU-rendered assertion (a pixel probe or the rendered parts list) that a teal-class part is drawn when the page is open. A collection-only check isn't enough.

**Also from this check (already posted above):** the preview shows nothing until the setup has an operation.

**Root cause found** (on the contributor's `test-519-520.camproj`, probing `incoming_shape` directly):
- **What it returns:** 115 200 triangles, all at **Z = 12**, spanning X/Y −30..30. That's the body's `display().surface`, the **top sheet only**, with no sides and no bottom.
- **Why it was invisible:** the part model spans Z 0..16 over the same footprint, so the whole teal sheet sits **inside the opaque part** in every view the tester tried.
- **Already pushed:** 6e370a86 makes the overlay draw after the traced stock as well. That's a real gap, but not the cause here.

**Fix (next push):** draw the incoming stock as a **closed body**:
- the top sheet, plus the bottom at the floor, plus the side walls around the body's footprint (Z −2..12 here);
- so it reads as a teal block whose top shows above or through the part, rather than a sheet buried in it;
- pinned by an app test that the mesh spans the full Z range of `incoming.min..max`.

Still a draft.

**Quick gate on f30280ed:** green apart from the no-GPU environment.
- **App suites:** 1505 pass. Named: setup_stock_view 3, setup_stock_source 6, setup_carry 9, stock_sim_document 9.
- **UI suites:** 496 pass. The only 3 failures are the known "No suitable graphics adapter" headless tests on this agent host.
- **Clippy:** clean.

**Still a draft:** it waits for the contributor's GUI re-check of the closed teal block, with the build `camcraft-ui-519c` (steps in their TESTING-GUI.md). I'll flag it ready once that passes.

**Help wanted: GPU verification.** The core agents' test runs can't reach a GPU, so every render test reports "No suitable graphics adapter found". If your machine renders GPU tests (Windows, Linux, or macOS outside a sandbox), please run this on the PR branch and post the output:
Run `cargo run --release -p camcraft-ui` and open a project where Setup2 takes "What Setup1 leaves behind". Open Setup2's settings page and hide the part model. You should see a translucent **teal block**: the stock Setup1 leaves. A screenshot is ideal.

Merged main to resolve conflicts (crates/ui/src/lib.rs, crates/ui/src/egui_app/setup_stock_pick.rs: keep both sides). Targeted gate: setup_stock_view 3/3, camcraft-ui incoming lib tests 3/3 pass; clippy -D warnings clean on camcraft-ui (lib and tests) and camcraft-app; the Incoming import main added is dropped because the PR's cache read no longer names the type (unused otherwise). Ready for a re-check (/resolve-conflicts check).
